items.plain: A prayer to God: root out the poverty in my heart; give me strength to bear joy and sorrow lightly, serve with love, stand by the poor, rise above trifles, and surrender my strength to your will.
items.core_idea: Ask God for strength to serve and surrender

items.plain: I thought my journey was over and my strength used up, but God's will in me has no end: when old words fail, new songs rise from the heart, and where old paths vanish, new country opens.
items.core_idea: When old paths end, new ones open

items.plain: My heart says to God again and again that it wants only Him; every other desire is empty. Even hidden deep inside me, even in my rebellion against His love, the cry is the same.
items.core_idea: Beneath every desire, the soul wants only God

items.plain: A prayer to God: when my heart is dry, come as mercy; when life loses grace, come as song; when work drowns me out, come as peace; when desire blinds me, come with light and thunder.
items.core_idea: Asking God to come in every hard state

items.plain: My heart has been dry for days, my God. Send a storm if you wish, even a deadly one, but take away this silent, burning despair, and let your grace bend down to me like a mother's tearful look.
items.core_idea: Rather a storm than silent despair

items.plain: Before I was ready, God, you entered my heart unnoticed and marked passing moments with eternity. You did not scorn my childish play; the steps I heard then echo now among the stars.
items.core_idea: God was present in ordinary moments all along

items.plain: My joy is to wait by the roadside, watching the seasons and the passing messengers, sure that the happy moment of seeing will come. Meanwhile I smile and sing alone, and the air fills with promise.
items.core_idea: Waiting with hope is itself a joy

items.plain: Have you not heard him coming? God comes always, every moment and every season. In April and in stormy July nights he comes; in sorrow after sorrow his steps press on my heart, and his touch makes my joy shine.
items.core_idea: God is always coming, in joy and sorrow

items.plain: All around us the morning was full of birdsong, flowers and golden light, but we hurried on without noticing. We did not sing, play, speak or smile; we only walked faster as time went by.
items.core_idea: Hurrying, we miss the beauty around us

items.plain: My companions mocked me and hurried on into the distance, crossing many lands. Their scorn did not move me; I let myself be lost, in a humiliation that was glad and a quiet delight.
items.core_idea: Letting others race ahead, content to rest

items.plain: I forgot what I was travelling for and gave myself up to the shade and songs. When I woke, God was standing beside me, smiling. I had feared the road to him was long and hard.
items.core_idea: God is found by resting, not striving

items.plain: A beggar hoped for riches from the passing King, but the King asked him for a gift. He gave one grain of corn. That night he found one grain of gold, and wept that he had not given everything.
items.core_idea: What we give to God returns as gold

items.plain: God's gift to me is pain, a burden that hurts and shames me, yet I will carry it as an honour. Now I fear nothing: death is my companion and God's sword cuts my bonds.
items.core_idea: Pain accepted as God's gift ends fear

items.plain: When you asked my name, God, I was ashamed; what had I done to be remembered? Yet the memory that I once gave you water for your thirst will stay sweet in my heart, as I sit and think.
items.core_idea: A small kindness to God is treasured

items.plain: Your heart is weary and your eyes still sleepy. Have you not heard that the flower is blooming in glory among the thorns? Wake up, and do not let the time go to waste.
items.core_idea: Wake up; do not waste the time

items.plain: Let my last song hold every kind of joy: the joy of wild grass, of life and death dancing together, of the storm that wakes everything, of tears sitting quietly with pain, and of giving everything away without a word.
items.core_idea: Joy holds life, death, storm and pain

items.plain: On the shore of endless worlds, children meet and play. Storms rage, ships sink and death is everywhere, yet the children play on.
items.core_idea: Children play on amid storm and death

items.plain: As a parent giving a child toys, songs, sweets and kisses, I understand why the world is full of colour, music, honey and morning delight: it is all a giving of love, like mine to my child.
items.core_idea: Loving a child reveals why the world is beautiful

fix.display_text:
When I bring to you coloured toys, my child, I understand why there is such a play of colours on clouds, on water, and why flowers are painted in tints—when I give coloured toys to you, my child.

When I sing to make you dance I truly know why there is music in leaves, and why waves send their chorus of voices to the heart of the listening earth—when I sing to make you dance.

When I bring sweet things to your greedy hands I know why there is honey in the cup of the flowers and why fruits are secretly filled with sweet juice—when I bring sweet things to your greedy hands.

When I kiss your face to make you smile, my darling, I surely understand what pleasure streams from the sky in morning light, and what delight that is that is which the summer breeze brings to my body—when I kiss you to make you smile.

items.plain: God, you have given me friends I did not know and homes not my own, and made strangers into brothers. Yet I fear leaving familiar shelter, forgetting that the old lives in the new and that you are there too.
items.core_idea: God is present in the new and unfamiliar

items.plain: Through birth and death, wherever God leads me, He is my one constant companion, tying my heart to the unfamiliar with joy. Whoever knows Him finds no one a stranger and no door shut.
items.core_idea: Knowing God, no one is a stranger

items.plain: The same life that flows in my veins flows through the whole world, in grass, leaves, flowers, and the tides of birth and death. Its touch makes me glorious; the pulse of ages dances in my blood.
items.core_idea: One life flows through me and the world

items.plain: Can you not rejoice in this rhythm, even be tossed and broken in its fearful joy? Everything rushes on without looking back; seasons, colours and scents pour past in a joy that gives itself away and dies every moment.
items.core_idea: Rejoice in life's endless rushing flow

items.plain: Freedom for me is not in renouncing the world but in a thousand bonds of delight. I will not close my senses: what I see, hear and touch will carry God's delight, and my desires will ripen into love.
items.core_idea: Freedom through delight, not renunciation

items.plain: Day after day, O God, I will stand before you face to face: in quiet solitude, in the crowded, toiling world, and, when my work is done, alone and silent.
items.core_idea: Standing before God in every moment

items.plain: I keep God at a respectful distance instead of holding Him close as my own. He is a brother among my brothers, yet I ignore them and do not share with them, and I shrink from plunging into life.
items.core_idea: Distance from people is distance from God

items.plain: When the gods sang that creation was perfect, one cried that a star was lost, and they have searched for her in grief ever since. But at night the stars whisper that the search is vain: perfection is unbroken.
items.core_idea: Nothing is truly lost; perfection remains whole

items.plain: If I do not meet God in this life, let me never forget that I have missed Him. Amid profits, rest and celebration, let me carry the ache of that loss, waking and dreaming.
items.core_idea: Keep the longing for God alive

items.plain: I used to grieve over idle days, but no time is lost, my God; you hold every moment, ripening seeds into fruit. I slept thinking all work had stopped, and woke to find my garden full of flowers.
items.core_idea: No time is lost in God's hands

items.plain: God has endless time and waits centuries to perfect one wild flower. We, poor in time, scramble and give it to anyone who demands it. Yet hurrying to God's gate at day's end, I find there is still time.
items.core_idea: God's patience means there is still time

items.plain: Mother, I will make you a necklace of my tears. Wealth and fame are yours to give or withhold, but my sorrow is truly mine, and when I offer it to you, you reward me with grace.
items.core_idea: Sorrow offered to God becomes grace

items.plain: The ache of separation fills the world and gives birth to countless shapes in the sky. This sorrow watches silently from star to star, sings in rainy darkness, and deepens into human love, longing, suffering and joy.
items.core_idea: Longing of separation shapes the world
items.extended_text:
It is the pang of separation that spreads throughout the world and gives birth to shapes innumerable in the infinite sky.

It is this sorrow of separation that gazes in silence all nights from star to star and becomes lyric among rustling leaves in rainy darkness of July.

It is this overspreading pain that deepens into loves and desires, into sufferings and joy in human homes; and this it is that ever melts and flows in songs through my poet’s heart.

items.plain: Death, God's servant, has come to my door with God's call. My heart is afraid, yet I will welcome him and honour him; when he leaves, only my lonely self will remain as my last offering to God.
items.core_idea: Welcoming death as God's messenger

items.plain: I search my small house for the one I lost and cannot find her. But God's house is infinite, where nothing vanishes. Plunge my emptied life into that fullness, so I may feel her lost touch in the whole universe.
items.core_idea: In God, nothing loved is truly lost

items.plain: When death knocks at your door, what will you give him? I will give him my whole life, all its sweetness and all its earnings; I will not let him leave empty-handed.
items.core_idea: Meet death with a life fully lived

items.plain: Death, you are life's final fulfilment; come and speak to me. I have lived all my joys and pains for you, and everything I am has flowed toward you. One look from you and my life is yours forever.
items.core_idea: Death as the fulfilment of life

items.plain: One day I will die and the world will go on. Thinking of that end, I see even the world's lowliest lives as precious. Let what I wanted pass; let me truly hold what I overlooked.
items.core_idea: Mortality reveals the worth of overlooked things

items.plain: I am leaving; say goodbye to me, my brothers. I give back my keys and claims and ask only for kind words. We were neighbours long, and I received more than I gave. Now I am ready.
items.core_idea: Parting with gratitude, ready for death

items.plain: Wish me well as I leave, friends; the dawn is bright and my path beautiful. I go with empty hands and a hopeful heart, dressed for a wedding, not a journey, and unafraid of the dangers.
items.core_idea: Facing death as a joyful journey

items.plain: I did not notice entering this life, yet the nameless mystery received me as my mother. Death will be that same unknown, already known; loving life, I will love death too, like a child moved to the other breast.
items.core_idea: Loving life, I shall love death too

items.plain: When I leave, let my parting word be that what I have seen is unsurpassed. I have tasted hidden sweetness and glimpsed and felt the formless One in this world of forms; if the end comes now, let it come.
items.core_idea: A parting word of gratitude for life

items.plain: I will honour God with the trophies of my defeat; I can never escape being conquered by Him. My pride will fall, my life will break its bonds in pain, my empty heart will sing, and stone will weep.
items.core_idea: Defeat by God breaks pride open

items.plain: When I let go of the helm, God takes it; my struggle is useless. So, my heart, accept defeat and sit still gladly. My lamps keep blowing out, so this time I will wait in the dark for God.
items.core_idea: Let go and let God steer

items.plain: In one bow to you, my God, let all my senses, my mind, my songs and my whole life bend toward you, like a heavy rain-cloud, or homesick cranes flying back to their mountain home.
items.core_idea: My whole life as one bow to God

items.plain: You can see a road as an obstacle between you and what you want, every step won by force. Or you can see it as the way to your goal, already part of it, giving you something with every step.
items.core_idea: The road is already part of the goal

items.plain: A person who does not feel kinship with the world lives as if in a prison of strange walls. One who meets the eternal spirit in everything is set free, finding the world's full meaning and harmony with all.
items.core_idea: Kinship with the world sets us free

items.plain: When people cut themselves off from nature and walk the tightrope of humanity alone, they must strain at every step to keep their balance, and when tired, they rail against Providence and secretly enjoy feeling unfairly treated.
items.core_idea: Cut off from nature, we strain and complain

items.plain: When a person's awareness reaches no further than their own human self, their deeper roots find no lasting soil, their spirit is always close to starving, and they replace real strength with rounds of stimulation.
items.core_idea: A narrow self swaps strength for stimulation

items.plain: Human greatness lies not in getting and achieving but in a soul that embraces all; callous habit and frantic work kill it. We are lovers, not slaves; love unites us with the Spirit, and pushing past others cuts us off.
items.core_idea: Our greatness and freedom lie in love

items.plain: Someone set on piling up riches, with an ego always swelling, cannot pass into the spiritual world of harmony; he stays shut inside the narrow walls of what he owns.
items.core_idea: Greed walls us off from the spirit

items.plain: Someone bent on enlarging himself treats everything else as unreal. To see the reality of all, we must be free of personal desire, ready to share others' burdens. A larger life means gaining by giving and growing in unity.
items.core_idea: Gain a larger life by giving

items.plain: Our selfish desires and egoistic impulses cloud our view of the soul, because they show only our narrow self. When we are aware of our soul, we see the inner being beyond the ego, close to the All.
items.core_idea: Selfish desire hides the soul

items.plain: Understanding finds something of ourselves in another, which gladdens us, but only partly. Love is complete: difference vanishes and the soul reaches into the infinite. So love is the highest bliss, showing we are one with the All.
items.core_idea: Love is complete union with the All

items.plain: It is ordinary, yet wonderful, that the joys and sorrows of those we love become ours, even more than ours. In them we have grown larger and touched the truth that holds the whole universe.
items.core_idea: Loving others makes us larger

items.plain: We must know for certain that we are spirit, by mastering self and rising above pride, greed and fear; loss and death cannot touch the soul. Like a chick breaking its shell, we must burst the dead shell of ego.
items.core_idea: Break the shell of ego to be free

items.plain: The Buddha tells Simha that he condemns only actions leading to evil, and preaches the ending only of pride, lust, evil thought and ignorance, never of forgiveness, love, charity and truth.
items.core_idea: The Buddha extinguishes vice, not love

items.plain: Until a person truly knows their soul, their poverty is bottomless, their wants endless, and the world a shifting illusion. Once the soul is realised, everything finds its place around a centre, and life becomes harmonious.
items.core_idea: Knowing the soul gives life a centre

fix.display_text: Man's poverty is abysmal, his wants are endless till he becomes truly conscious of his soul. Till then, the world to him is in a state of continual flux--a phantasm that is and is not. For a man who has realised his soul there is a determinate centre of the universe around which all else can find its proper place, and from thence only can he draw and enjoy the blessedness of a harmonious life.

items.plain: The early earth was scattered heat until a central force drew it into a beautiful whole. So with the soul: driven by blind passions we give nothing truly, but centred by self-restraint, our impressions become wisdom and impulses love.
items.core_idea: A centred soul turns impulse into love

items.plain: We are miserable because we live as creatures of a narrow, blind self, loud with discord. Discontent, regret for the past and worry about the future trouble us because we have not found our souls.
items.core_idea: Misery comes from living only as self

items.plain: In sin, we crave pleasures only because passion makes them look desirable, and want things only because greed makes them look great. These distortions break our harmony and leave us without true values, pulled about by competing claims.
items.core_idea: Passion and greed distort what we value

items.plain: People long to express themselves fully, and that leads them to chase wealth and power. But piling things up is not fulfilment; it is the inner light that reveals who we are, not outward things.
items.core_idea: Accumulation is not fulfilment

items.plain: Our real misery is that we have not fully emerged; we are hidden from ourselves, lost in our own desires, unable to feel beyond our surroundings, our greater self blotted out.
items.core_idea: Lost in desire, our greater self is hidden

items.plain: A river has banks, but it is not just banks; the banks push its water forward. A towing rope binds a boat, yet it also pulls the boat ahead. Limits are not the whole meaning.
items.core_idea: Limits can move us forward

items.plain: What is remarkable is not that the world has obstacles and suffering, but that it has law and order, beauty and joy, goodness and love.
items.core_idea: The wonder is goodness, not suffering

items.plain: Pain is the feeling of our limits; it is not a permanent part of life or an end in itself, as joy is. To meet pain is to learn that it has no place in what truly lasts.
items.core_idea: Pain passes; joy is lasting

items.plain: Life as a whole does not take death seriously; it keeps playing, building and loving. Death frightens us only when isolated, like cloth seen under a microscope as holes. Death is not the final reality and does not stain existence.
items.core_idea: Death does not darken life as a whole

items.plain: A child learning to walk fails over and over, which would look cruel if we watched only briefly. But a joy drives the child on, and it thinks less of its falls than of its moments of balance.
items.core_idea: Joy carries us through repeated failure

items.plain: Viewed narrowly, our failures loom large, but life leads us to a wider view. Within us is a hope, a faith in the infinite, that accepts no limitation as permanent, claims oneness with God, and keeps coming true.
items.core_idea: Hope in the infinite outruns our failures

items.plain: If existence were evil, no philosopher would be needed to prove it. Arguing it is like accusing a man of suicide while he stands alive in front of you; existence itself shows it is not evil.
items.core_idea: Existence itself proves it is not evil

items.plain: For those who live for others or an ideal, pain matters less; pleasure serves oneself, goodness serves all. A pitcher of seawater is heavy, yet in the sea you feel no weight: living for self makes pleasure and pain heavy.
items.core_idea: Living for others lightens pain

fix.display_text: To the man who lives for an idea, for his country, for the good of humanity, life has an extensive meaning, and to that extent pain becomes less important to him. To live the life of goodness is to live the life of all. Pleasure is for one's own self, but goodness is concerned with the happiness of all humanity and for all time. From the point of view of the good, pleasure and pain appear in a different meaning; so much so, that pleasure may be shunned, and pain be courted in its place, and death itself be made welcome as giving a higher value to life. From these higher standpoints of a man's life, the standpoints of the good, pleasure and pain lose their absolute value. Martyrs prove it in history, and we prove it every day in our life in our little martyrdoms. When we take a pitcherful of water from the sea it has its weight, but when we take a dip into the sea itself a thousand pitchersful of water flow above our head, and we do not feel their weight. We have to carry the pitcher of self with our strength; and so, while on the plane of selfishness pleasure and pain have their full weight, on the moral plane they are so much lightened that the man who has reached it appears to us almost superhuman in his patience under crushing trials, and his forbearance in the face of malignant persecution.

items.plain: A strong imagination is closer to truth, and a strong individuality widens toward the universal. A personality's greatness lies in its universal content, just as a lake's depth is measured by its water, not the size of its hollow.
items.core_idea: Greatness lies in content, not size

items.plain: When my boat's mast stuck under a bridge, neither mast, bridge nor river gave way. That is exactly why I can rely on them. Things are what they are; we can know them because our wishes are not their law.
items.core_idea: Our wishes are not the world's law

items.plain: When the individual in us resists the universal, we shrink and suffer; success becomes failure and fulfilled desire leaves us poorer. Seeking special privilege, we live behind barricades and complain of unhappiness, though the universal spirit waits to give joy.
items.core_idea: Seeking special privilege makes us miserable

items.plain: Life's key lesson is not that pain exists, but that we can use it well and even turn it into joy. No one would give up the right to suffer, for it is the right to be human.
items.core_idea: We can transform pain into joy

items.plain: A poor mother was hurt when a rich relative offered to take her son, for a mother's trouble is hers by right of love. Freedom is not being spared trouble, but taking it on and making it part of joy.
items.core_idea: Freedom is taking on trouble, not escaping it

items.plain: Ignorance makes us think the self is complete, so we live for it and are disappointed, like clutching road dust to reach a destination. The self passes on; living for its pleasure is a fire without bread, burning itself out.
items.core_idea: Living for the self alone ends in emptiness

items.plain: We become free when we reach our truest nature, as an artist is freed from imitation and the need for applause by finding their ideal. Religion's role is not to destroy our nature but to fulfil it.
items.core_idea: Religion should fulfil our nature, not destroy it

items.plain: A seed is free when it fulfils its nature by becoming a tree; failing to do so is its prison. The sacrifice that brings fulfilment is not death but throwing off the bonds that hold us back.
items.core_idea: Freedom is fulfilling one's true nature

items.plain: A lamp clings to its oil, separate and miserly, but once lit it connects with everything and gladly spends its oil on the flame. Our self is like that lamp: hoarding keeps it dark; lit, it gives everything.
items.core_idea: The self, like a lamp, shines by giving
items.extended_text:
The lamp contains its oil, which it holds securely in its close grasp and guards from the least loss. Thus is it separate from all other objects around it and is miserly. But when lighted it finds its meaning at once; its relation with all things far and near is established, and it freely sacrifices its fund of oil to feed the flame.

Such a lamp is our self. So long as it hoards its possessions it keeps itself dark, its conduct contradicts its true purpose. When it finds illumination it forgets itself in a moment, holds the light high, and serves it with everything it has; for therein is its revelation.

items.plain: Love is its own end. Everything else makes us ask why and want a reason, but when we say we love, there is no room for why; love is its own final answer.
items.core_idea: Love needs no reason

items.plain: A selfish person gives only under compulsion, like tearing unripe fruit from a branch. One who loves gives with joy, as a tree lets go of ripe fruit. Love loosens our grip on possessions, and giving them away fulfils us.
items.core_idea: Love makes giving a joy

items.plain: The Gita says we must act, for action shows our nature, but only free action shows it fully; work driven by want or fear hides it. Like a mother serving her children, true freedom is freedom in action, through love.
items.core_idea: True freedom is acting out of love

items.plain: Repulsion only separates. Love both separates and unites, but the separation only seems real and the union is the final truth, as when a father tosses his child up: it looks like letting go, but is the opposite.
items.core_idea: In love, separation only seems real

items.plain: Work done only out of necessity is makeshift, abandoned once the need passes. Work that comes from joy takes on something immortal, because the immortal in us gives it permanence.
items.core_idea: Work born of joy endures

items.plain: To live, the self must keep changing and growing, dying and living at once. Refusing that change, fixing the self in place and treating its limits as final, is really choosing death.
items.core_idea: Refusing to change is a kind of death

items.plain: A tyrant crushes his slaves' will because his self-interest is not free and cannot bear freedom in others; he actually depends on them. A lover needs two free wills, for love is fulfilled in harmony between freedom and freedom.
items.core_idea: Love needs two free wills

items.plain: The self must be born again every moment, breaking through the illusions that crust it over, make it seem old and weigh it down with death.
items.core_idea: Be born anew every moment

items.plain: Our life, like a river, meets its banks not to be shut in but to discover again its endless opening to the sea. Like a poem keeping its metre, its limits express an inner freedom rather than silence it.
items.core_idea: Our limits open toward freedom

items.plain: It is said that the unrighteous prosper and defeat their enemies for a while, but in the end are cut off at the root. To grow into true greatness, our roots must reach deep into the universal.
items.core_idea: Greatness needs roots in the universal

items.plain: A child's play would be a horror if he could not return to his mother, and our pride in being someone will curse us if we cannot give it up in love.
items.core_idea: Pride must be surrendered in love

items.plain: Literature follows grammar yet is pure joy and freedom. A poem's laws are its wings, carrying it to freedom, not weighing it down. Law is the first step to freedom, and beauty, built on law, unites limit and liberty.
items.core_idea: Law is the first step to freedom

items.plain: Formless joy has to create and take shape: the singer's joy becomes a song, the poet's a poem. As creators, people keep making forms, and these flow from their overflowing joy.
items.core_idea: Creation flows from overflowing joy

items.plain: Our individual soul is separate from the supreme soul through the fullness of love, not estrangement. So falsehood, suffering and evil are not fixed: the soul can defy and overcome them, and turn them into new power and beauty.
items.core_idea: The soul can transform evil into beauty

items.plain: The soul travels from law to love, discipline to freedom, morality to spirit. The Buddha taught self-restraint and moral discipline, a full acceptance of law; but law is not the end, and mastering it lets us go beyond it.
items.core_idea: Master the law to go beyond it

items.plain: Lack of love is a kind of numbness, since love is consciousness made perfect. We fail to understand because we do not love. Love is not just a feeling; it is truth, the joy at the root of all creation.
items.core_idea: We do not understand because we do not love

items.plain: Love gives endlessly, but its gifts matter most when they lead us to the giver, and that needs love in us. Without love we value gifts only for their passing use; with love, even a small token has lasting worth.
items.core_idea: With love, a token outlasts any use

items.plain: How do we receive this world, a perfect gift of joy? We rush to exploit it for power and riches. Using it only, we cheapen it and miss its truth, like a greedy child eating pages of a precious book.
items.core_idea: Using the world only, we miss its worth

items.plain: People are useful to each other, but each is also a spirit, known truly only through love. Valued by market worth, a person is easily wronged. Seen as spirit, they are our own: cruelty to them is cruelty to ourselves.
items.core_idea: Seen as spirit, others are our own

items.plain: Our desires limit our growth and give rise to sin, which separates us from God. Sin is not a single act but an attitude: that our goal is finite, our self the final truth, and we are not all one.
items.core_idea: Sin is believing we are separate

items.plain: A civilisation should be judged not by the power it has built, but by how far its laws and institutions express love of humanity. Its first and last test: does it see people more as spirits than machines?
items.core_idea: Judge a civilisation by its love of humanity

items.plain: Seen through our desires, the world looks small. It meets our needs, but our bond with it goes deeper: loving life is wishing to stay connected with it. That bond is love, with threads reaching from earth to stars.
items.core_idea: Our bond with the world is love

items.plain: The spirit finds its larger self in the whole world and knows it is immortal. Walled in by self it dies again and again, but one with all it cannot die. Feeling the world's soul within, a person is free.
items.core_idea: United with all, the spirit is free

items.plain: Only love is both movement and rest. The heart keeps moving until it finds love, then rests; yet that rest is intense activity, where perfect stillness and endless energy meet.
items.core_idea: Love is motion and rest at once

items.plain: In love, loss and gain are reconciled; giving counts as gaining. In creation, which is God's great self-giving, the lover keeps giving himself up to find himself in love. Love joins letting go and receiving into one.
items.core_idea: In love, giving is gaining

items.plain: Hunger makes demands, but it is not the last word for a human being. Some have defied it to show the soul is not ruled by want or pain, and to live humanly we all resist it daily.
items.core_idea: Need is not the last word

items.plain: What finally moves us is joy, not compulsion. Joy is everywhere: in grass, sky, spring and winter, in the body, in living, learning and fighting evil. It is surplus, unnecessary, often defying the demands of necessity.
items.core_idea: Joy, not compulsion, moves us

fix.display_text: Compulsion is not indeed the final appeal to man, but joy is. And joy is everywhere; it is in the earth's green covering of grass; in the blue serenity of the sky; in the reckless exuberance of spring; in the severe abstinence of grey winter; in the living flesh that animates our bodily frame; in the perfect poise of the human figure, noble and upright; in living; in the exercise of all our powers; in the acquisition of knowledge; in fighting evils; in dying for gains we never can share. Joy is there everywhere; it is superfluous, unnecessary; nay, it very often contradicts the most peremptory behests of necessity.

items.plain: Only those who know that joy expresses itself through law can go beyond law. The bonds remain, but become the very shape of freedom. A freed soul gladly accepts bonds, feeling in each the infinite energy that delights in creating.
items.core_idea: For the free, bonds become freedom

items.plain: Without bonds, in reckless licence, the soul is not free but hurt and cut off from the infinite. Fallen into temptation, it cries like a child dropped from its mother's arms, begging God to bind it in His law.
items.core_idea: Without bonds, the soul loses its freedom

fix.display_text: As a matter of fact, where there are no bonds, where there is the madness of license, the soul ceases to be free. There is its hurt; there is its separation from the infinite, its agony of sin. Whenever at the call of temptation the soul falls away from the bondage of law, then, like a child deprived of the support of its mother's arms, it cries out, Smite me not! "Bind me," it prays, "oh, bind me in the bonds of thy law; bind me within and without; hold me tight; let me in the clasp of thy law be bound up together with thy joy; protect me by thy firm hold from the deadly laxity of sin."

items.plain: Freedom is not in vagueness; obscurity is the worst bondage. Seeds sprout and ideas seek form to escape it, and the soul keeps creating new kinds of action, even unneeded ones, because it wants to see and realise itself.
items.core_idea: The soul seeks freedom through action

items.plain: When people turn a jungle into a garden or bring order to society, the beauty and goodness they free outside are their own soul's, which cannot otherwise be free within. The more they free in action, the greater they become.
items.core_idea: Freeing good outside frees the soul within

items.plain: Those who have realised the soul never lament life's sorrow or the bondage of work. They cling to life until the fruit is ripe, express themselves fully in work, and walk upright through joys and sorrows, undaunted by pain.
items.core_idea: The realised hold fast to life

items.plain: No creature works as hard as humans, building and tearing down, making laws, thinking, suffering, even taking on new troubles willingly. We have found that we are greater than our present, and that standing still destroys life's true purpose.
items.core_idea: We are greater than our present

fix.display_text: No creature has to work so hard as man; he has been impelled to contrive for himself a vast field of action in society; and in this field he is for ever building up and pulling down, making and unmaking laws, piling up heaps of material, and incessantly thinking, seeking and suffering. In this field he has fought his mightiest battles, gained continual new life, made death glorious, and, far from evading troubles, has willingly and continually taken up the burden of fresh trouble. He has discovered the truth that he is not complete in the cage of his immediate surroundings, that he is greater than his present, and that while to stand still in one place may be comforting, the arrest of life destroys his true function and the real purpose of his existence.

items.plain: We gain the joy of freedom only by fully submitting to truth, like a harp string. Only when tightly strung does it make music and find freedom; loosening it would not free it, only tuning it to true pitch.
items.core_idea: Like a tuned string, bonds make music

items.plain: Whoever tries to reach God by fleeing the world, where does he expect to meet Him? Flight leads only to nothing; the coward finds Him nowhere. We must dare to say we are reaching God right here, right now.
items.core_idea: Meet God here and now, not by fleeing

items.plain: We need holidays because we find no joy in work. A river's joy is in flowing, a fire's in blazing, a flower's in its scent. Work overwhelms us because we do not give ourselves to it fully and joyfully.
items.core_idea: Give yourself fully to work to find joy

items.plain: A prayer to God: give us the strength to love our whole life, its joys and sorrows, gains and losses, to see and hear your universe fully and work in it vigorously, to live fully, taking and giving bravely.
items.core_idea: Pray for strength to love all of life

items.plain: Things that give us no joy are burdens to shed, tools that weigh on us once used, or passers-by soon forgotten. Something is fully our own only when it is a joy to us.
items.core_idea: Only what brings joy is truly ours

items.plain: Truth is everywhere, so everything can be known. Beauty is everywhere, so everything can give us joy.
items.core_idea: Beauty everywhere means joy everywhere

items.plain: Our sense of truth shows us the law in creation; our sense of beauty shows us its harmony. Knowing nature's laws gives us power; knowing the laws of our moral nature gives us mastery over ourselves and freedom.
items.core_idea: Knowing our moral law makes us free

items.plain: Alone in the silent night I heard the eternal singer. Falling asleep, I thought that even in sleep life's dance goes on in my body, heart and blood keeping time with the stars, every atom vibrating to the master's touch.
items.core_idea: Life's dance continues even in sleep

items.plain: When the soul longs for God, it does not want to add one more valuable thing to its belongings; endless adding is wearisome. Seeking God, the soul seeks its final escape from this endless gathering and heaping.
items.core_idea: Seeking God is escape from endless getting

items.plain: See everything in the universe as wrapped in God. Enjoy what He gives you, and do not let greed for wealth that is not yours take hold of your mind.
items.core_idea: Enjoy God's gifts; do not covet

items.plain: We do not have to buy morning light from a shop; we open our eyes and it is there. In the same way, we only need to give ourselves up to find that Brahma is everywhere.
items.core_idea: Brahma is everywhere, like morning light

items.plain: The Upanishads say: be lost in Brahma like an arrow buried in its target. Knowing Brahma surrounds us is not mere concentration but the aim of our whole life; in every act let us feel the infinite energy and rejoice.
items.core_idea: Live wholly conscious of the infinite

items.plain: In deep love, having and not having always go together. A Vaishnava lover tells the beloved: I seem to have gazed at your face since birth, yet my eyes still hunger; held you for ages, yet am not satisfied.
items.core_idea: Deep love is never fully satisfied

fix.display_text: In all our deeper love getting and non-getting run ever parallel. In one of our Vaishnava lyrics the lover says to his beloved: "I feel as if I have gazed upon the beauty of thy face from my birth, yet my eyes are hungry still: as if I have kept thee pressed to my heart for millions of years, yet my heart is not satisfied."

items.plain: Our wish for wealth is not for a set sum but for something unlimited, and even fleeting pleasures are brief touches of the eternal. Our tragedy is trying to reach the infinite by endlessly adding rungs to a finite ladder.
items.core_idea: We cannot reach the infinite by adding more

items.plain: Renunciation is the soul's deepest truth. Saying it does not want something because it is above it, the soul speaks its highest truth, like a girl who outgrows her doll and throws it away. Bondage to lesser things is misery.
items.core_idea: We are greater than what we own

items.plain: A flying bird feels with every wingbeat that the sky is boundless, and that is its joy. A cage meets its needs but no more, and it cannot rejoice. It is glad only having far more than it needs.
items.core_idea: Joy needs more than the necessary

items.plain: Lasting happiness comes not from getting but from giving ourselves to something greater: country, humanity, God. Until an idea claims our all, life is mean. The great prophets offer such ideas, and in giving we find joy and freedom.
items.core_idea: Happiness lies in giving ourselves to something greater

fix.display_text: Man's abiding happiness is not in getting anything but in giving himself up to what is greater than himself, to ideas which are larger than his individual life, the idea of his country, of humanity, of God. They make it easier for him to part with all that he has, not excepting his life. His existence is miserable and sordid till he finds some great idea which can truly claim his all, which can release him from all attachment to his belongings. Buddha and Jesus, and all our great prophets, represent such great ideas. They hold before us opportunities for surrendering our all. When they bring forth their divine alms-bowl we feel we cannot help giving, and we find that in giving is our truest joy and liberation, for it is uniting ourselves to that extent with the infinite.

items.plain: A human being is not finished but still becoming. What we are is small; stopping there forever would be hell. What we are yet to be is infinite: our heaven. Our present grasps; our becoming hungers for more.
items.core_idea: We are not finished; we are becoming

items.plain: The rushing stream sings that it will become the sea; this is truth, not pride. It serves fields and towns along its way but stays separate; it can never become a forest or town. But it becomes the sea.
items.core_idea: The river's destiny is the sea

items.plain: A poem delights when the reader grasps the idea running through it; without that, endless images weary. The soul's progress is the same: grasp its infinite idea and every movement has meaning; lose it, and existence seems aimless and monstrous.
items.core_idea: Life has meaning when seen as a whole

items.plain: Words and the mind fall back, unable to reach Brahma, but whoever knows Him through His joy is free of all fear.
items.core_idea: Knowing Brahma's joy frees us from fear

items.plain: The intellect keeps us apart from what we know, but love knows by becoming one with it. This knowing is immediate and beyond doubt, like knowing ourselves, only more so.
items.core_idea: Love knows by becoming one

items.plain: We feel we have not reached our goal; however hard we work, we never arrive. Like a child bored with its dolls, the heart keeps saying: not this, not this. But what is the other? Where is the farther shore?
items.core_idea: The heart keeps longing for something beyond

items.plain: My self toils for a home it calls its own, and suffers until it calls that home God's. Grasping what belongs to all, it hurts and is hurt. Once it calls its work God's, nothing changes, yet it crosses over.
items.core_idea: Offer your work to God and be carried across

items.plain: Where can I meet God except in my home made His and my work turned into His? Leaving home or work, I will not find Him. God lives in me and I in Him; apart, both are nothing.
items.core_idea: Meet God in your own home and work

items.plain: The earth's tears are what keep her smiles blooming.
items.core_idea: Sorrow nourishes joy

items.plain: If you weep over missing the sun, you will also miss seeing the stars.
items.core_idea: Grieving what's gone can blind you to what's here

items.plain: We once dreamed we were strangers, and woke to find we were dear to each other.
items.core_idea: We are closer than we think

items.plain: The sorrow in my heart grows quiet and peaceful, like evening settling among still trees.
items.core_idea: Sorrow can settle into peace

items.plain: Do not place your love on a cliff edge just because it is high.
items.core_idea: Do not love something for its height

items.plain: You cannot see what you really are; what you see is only your shadow.
items.core_idea: Our true self is unseen by us

items.plain: I cannot pick the best; the best picks me.
items.core_idea: The best chooses us

items.plain: People who carry their lamp behind them cast their own shadows ahead of them.
items.core_idea: Light behind us darkens the path ahead

items.plain: Life is the constant surprise that I exist at all.
items.core_idea: Existing at all is a constant wonder

items.plain: Rest belongs to work the way eyelids belong to eyes.
items.core_idea: Rest is part of work

items.plain: A human being is born a child, and our power is the power to grow.
items.core_idea: Our power is growth

items.plain: Beauty, find yourself in love, not in your mirror's flattery.
items.core_idea: Beauty is found in love, not vanity

items.plain: Life gains its wealth from what the world asks of it, and its worth from what love asks of it.
items.core_idea: Love, not the world, gives life worth

items.plain: A dried-up riverbed gets no thanks for the water it once carried.
items.core_idea: Past service is soon forgotten

items.plain: The bird wishes to be a cloud, and the cloud wishes to be a bird.
items.core_idea: Everyone longs to be something else

items.plain: The waterfall sings that it finds its song when it finds its freedom.
items.core_idea: Freedom brings out our song

items.plain: Do not blame the food when you are the one without appetite.
items.core_idea: The fault may lie in us

items.plain: You smiled and talked to me about nothing, and I felt this was what I had long been waiting for.
items.core_idea: Simple closeness is what we wait for

items.plain: He has turned his weapons into gods; when his weapons win, he himself is defeated.
items.core_idea: Worshipping force defeats us

items.plain: The stars are not afraid of looking as small as fireflies.
items.core_idea: True greatness does not fear seeming small

items.plain: A mind that is sharp but narrow catches on every detail and never moves forward.
items.core_idea: Sharpness without breadth gets stuck

items.plain: People do not show who they are in their history; they struggle upward through it.
items.core_idea: We rise through history, not in it

items.plain: We meet and draw close like seagulls and waves; then the gulls fly off, the waves roll away, and we part.
items.core_idea: Meetings are brief, then we part

items.plain: My day is over, and I am like a boat pulled up on the beach, listening to the tide's dance music in the evening.
items.core_idea: Resting peacefully at the end of the day
